summary.text: Jack Reed is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to the U.S. Senate from Rhode Island, where he has served since 1997. A Cranston native and West Point graduate, he served as an Army officer and taught at the academy, practiced banking and securities law, and served in the Rhode Island State Senate and the U.S. House before his election to the Senate in 1996. He is the ranking member of the Armed Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Reed was born and raised in Cranston, Rhode Island, according to his Senate office, where his father, Joe, was a World War II veteran who became custodial supervisor of the city's school system and his mother, Mary, was a homemaker; Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Providence, in 1949. He attended St. Matthew's Elementary School and graduated from La Salle Academy in Providence.

He graduated from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1971, earned a master's degree in public policy from Harvard's Kennedy School in 1973, and received a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1982.

Reed served in the 82nd Airborne Division as an infantry platoon leader, company commander and battalion staff officer, then taught economics and international relations at West Point as an associate professor. He resigned from active duty as a captain in August 1979 and served in the Army Reserves until June 1991, leaving as a major.
After law school he practiced first at Sutherland, Asbill & Brennan and then at Edwards & Angell in Providence, specializing in banking and securities law and doing pro bono work for Amos House.

Reed served three terms in the Rhode Island State Senate (1985-1991) and, after his election in 1990, three terms in the U.S. House of Representatives (1991-1997), representing Rhode Island's 2nd District.

In 1996 he was elected to the U.S. Senate to succeed Claiborne Pell. He is ranking member of the Armed Services Committee and a senior member of the Appropriations Committee, and according to his Senate office he was part of the bipartisan working group that drafted the CARES Act.
He and his wife, Julia Hart Reed, have a daughter, Emily.
